evidence.1: They follow laws that require transparency about their data practices.
evidence.2: They base their actions on contracts, customer requests
evidence.4: legal requirements, and their own interests

unsupported.quote: They aim to act responsibly and only when it’s necessary.
unsupported.claim: Promises the company processes data only when necessary; the passage relies on consent in some other cases and on legitimate interests in many cases, with no necessity limit.

evidence.1: Companies in some places are required to inform you about how they use your data.
evidence.3: You can consent to certain uses, like providing services or marketing.
evidence.4: Companies may use your data to protect their business, customers, and property.
evidence.6: They might also use your data to comply with laws

unsupported.quote: This data includes things like your name, email, and event tickets.
unsupported.claim: Invents name and email as examples of the data; the passage mentions event tickets only as an example of contract-based processing.
Presents providing services and marketing as uses that rest on your consent; the passage bases providing services on contract and marketing on legitimate interests.
Invents protecting data security as an example of legal compliance.

evidence.1: Some jurisdictions require us to disclose the legal grounds for using or disclosing your personal data.

evidence.3: Because you gave consent, either implied or express.
evidence.4: Because it supports our legitimate interests, such as customer service, marketing, protecting customers, improving our business, handling legal matters, and assisting business partners in marketing.
evidence.6: To comply with legal obligations, including protecting vital interests

unsupported.quote: These are the only grounds we rely on, and we do not use any other reasons.
unsupported.claim: Adds an explicit promise that no other grounds are ever used.

evidence.3: We also rely on your consent, when required by law or in other cases.
evidence.4: In many situations, we use personal data based on our legitimate interests, such as improving our services, marketing, customer support, and protecting people and property.

evidence.3: They also use your data when you’ve agreed (either by actively consenting or by not opting out) or when required by law.
evidence.4: if those needs don’t outweigh your rights or freedoms

unsupported.claim: Defines implied consent as not opting out, which the passage does not say.

unsupported.quote: They sometimes share your data with business partners for their marketing efforts
unsupported.claim: Says data is shared with business partners; the passage says only that it may be processed for partners' legitimate interests.

unsupported.quote: like reporting taxes or responding to legal requests
unsupported.claim: Invents tax reporting and responding to legal requests as examples of legal compliance.
Adds that vital-interest processing happens only rarely.

evidence.4: provided those interests do not override your fundamental rights or interests
